text:
Avery: FYI ran into a weird edge when installing redwoodctl on a macbook where my dotfiles live on a symlinked path (/Users/avery -> /Volumes/dev/dotfiles). Installer succeeded but later `redwoodctl auth login` kept failing because it couldn't atomically write profiles.json.
Rae: Did the pkg create a symlink or follow it?
Avery: It followed it but created a broken permission state: the containing dir was root-owned because the pkg postinstall ran under a different context for the symlink target. Error in debug log: `fs: mkdir /Users/avery/.redwood: permission denied` even though the parent exists.
OpsBot: Typical symptom: auth flow completes in browser but CLI falls back to ephemeral session and users see sporadic 401s.
Avery: Workaround I used: `sudo chown -R $(whoami) /Volumes/dev/dotfiles/.redwood` then `redwoodctl auth login --reinit`. But that's awful to expect from users.
Rae: We should: (1) make installer detect when home is a symlink or on a nonstandard FS and emit a friendly warning, (2) add a `redwoodctl install --sanity-check` that verifies writability, atomic write behavior, and prints suggested fixes, and (3) log a single-line troubleshooting hint when the CLI falls back to ephemeral session.
DocTeam: Agreed. I'll add a small paragraph to the installer docs and the quickstart about symlinked homes and network/mounted volumes. Also propose an opt-in interactive installer prompt that asks to fix perms automatically when safe.
Avery: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/5899 — "installer: detect symlinked/non-POSIX homes; add --sanity-check and clearer fallback messages" (label: devex).
OpsBot: Issue created and assigned to Installer team.
Rae: Also add a CI note: golden images that mount dotfiles into home should run `redwoodctl install --sanity-check` as part of bake to catch these early.
Avery: Happy to draft the small repro & Dockerfile/macos pkg steps. Closing loop here — thanks everyone :raised_hands:
